newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish FinMin says spending ceiling to remain.
newsitem.headline: Swedish FinMin says spending ceiling to remain.

text.p: Sweden's minority social democratic government will not change its budget spending ceiling for 1997, 1998 and 1999, Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday.
Asbrink added the spending ceiling for year 2000 is set to be 744 billion crowns.
The expenditure ceiling for 1997 is set at 723 billion crowns, 720 billion for 1998 and 735 billion for 1999.
The spending ceiling includes the central government, the social insurance sector and municipalities. Treasury bills are excluded as they cannot be changed short term.
